x: Drawn in the first heat, he lined up alongside the Olympic 200 metre champion Don Quarrie of Jamaica and as the runners burst from their blocks Ernie's pick-up seemed the best and for a while he appeared to be shading Quarrie.
Ernest Obeng of Ghana and Belgrave Harriers beats Olympic 200 metre Champion Don Quarrie of Jamaica over 100 metres at the Philips Night of Athletics, Crystal Palace May 24th.

Lined up for the start of the Philips International Games 100 metres on May 24th were two fairly highly rated Americans, Britain's number two sprinter Mike McFarlane and the Olympic 200 metre champion Don Quarrie of Jamaica.

On June 29th at Porsgrunn in the Telemark Games he defeated Jamaica's Don Quarrie and the U.K's Drew McMaster - all 10.2 - and then two days later in Oslo at the world famous Bislett Stadium, headed the U.K. trio of Sharp, McMaster and McFarlane to win in 10.47.

No finer compliment can be paid to our two than to list a handful of previous winners of these titles. 220yds/200m - Eric Liddell, McDonald Bailey, Steve Riddick, Don Quarrie, Mel Lattany and Stanley Floyd.
